# Microservices Interview Questions

> About 100 questions with short model answers, from service boundaries to sagas and migration. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Cheat sheets

- [Common Mistakes in Microservices Interviews](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/common-mistakes.md): Most candidates know the definitions.
- [Monolith vs Microservices](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/monolith-vs-microservices.md): A monolith is one application built and deployed as a single unit.
- [Microservices Patterns at a Glance](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/patterns-at-a-glance.md): A pattern is a named, reusable solution to a problem that appears in many systems.
- [Saga: Choreography vs Orchestration](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/saga-choreography-vs-orchestration.md): A saga is a sequence of local transactions across services, with a compensating transaction to undo each step if a later one fails.
- [Synchronous vs Asynchronous Communication](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/synchronous-vs-asynchronous-communication.md): In synchronous communication the caller waits for the reply before it continues.
- [Two-Week Preparation Plan](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/cheat-sheets/two-week-plan.md): This plan covers every topic in this repository in 14 days at about one hour a day.

## Questions

- [API Gateway and Service Discovery: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/api-gateway-and-service-discovery.md): An API gateway is the single entry point that clients call instead of calling services directly.
- [Communication Between Services: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/communication.md): Services communicate in two ways: a synchronous call, where the caller waits for a reply, and asynchronous messaging, where the caller hands a message to a broker and continues.
- [Data Consistency and Sagas: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/data-consistency-and-sagas.md): When each service owns its database, one business operation can no longer run inside one database transaction.
- [Deployment and Testing: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/deployment-and-testing.md): Independent deployment is the main benefit of microservices: one team releases one service without waiting for any other team.
- [Migrating From a Monolith: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/migrating-from-a-monolith.md): A monolith is an application that is built and deployed as one unit.
- [Observability: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/observability.md): Observability is the ability to explain what a system is doing from the data it emits.
- [Resilience: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/resilience.md): Resilience is the ability of a system to keep serving requests when one of its parts fails or slows down.
- [Security: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/security.md): A monolith has one entry point to protect.
- [Service Boundaries: Interview Questions](https://github.com/design-gurus/microservices-interview-questions/blob/main/questions/service-boundaries.md): A service boundary is the line that decides which data and behavior one service owns.
